1	\section{Discussion}
2	\label{sec:discussion}
3	
4	The results establish three insights that frame CIVO as a structural vulnerability of flat temporal conditioning in imagination-based RL. Full mechanistic analysis, gradient decomposition, and seed-divergence discussion are in Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix_analysis}.
5	
6	\paragraph{CIVO mechanism.}
7	The RSSM reward head develops a $2.78\times$ prediction gap between $\dt{=}1$ and $\dt{=}2$ under trained conditioning (Table~\ref{tab:rssm_fidelity}), providing the systematic bias that the critic internalizes and the actor exploits, creating a four-stage feedback loop analogous to delusional bias \citep{lu2018nondelusional} but model-induced rather than policy-class-induced.  Full-pathway SGS (exp\_018) targets the gradient channel that maintains this bias, yet yields mixed results (50\% collapse prevention), indicating that CIVO involves mechanisms beyond gradient-mediated co-adaptation of the temporal embedding.
8	
9	\paragraph{Gradient decomposition and intervention design.}
10	\label{sec:gradient_evolution_main}
11	Gradient decomposition (Figure~\ref{fig:gradient_decomp}, Table~\ref{tab:gradient_decomposition}) reveals a non-obvious structure: the reward head provides the largest gradient contribution to $e_{\Delta t}$ (49.0\% at 55K, 38.1\% at 112K), yet reward-only SGS (exp\_016e) is functionally insufficient (NVE $10.42\times$, collapse).  The observation decoder channel contributes the smallest share (16.3\% at 55K, 21.5\% at 112K) but encodes the critical $\dt$-specific spatial predictions that generate the RSSM fidelity gap.  Full-pathway SGS, which removes observation decoder \emph{and} reward gradients from $e_{\Delta t}$, \sgsclaim{} (seed~1: peak NVE $\sgsnve{}\times$, eval \sgseval{}; seed~2: collapsed, eval 40.8).  The 50\% prevention rate confirms that the observation decoder gradient pathway is causally involved but reveals that CIVO's feedback loop has redundant mechanisms not fully captured by gradient decomposition.
12	
13	\paragraph{Why does $\dt$-conditioning succeed in MPC but fail in imagination-based AC?}
14	TAWM \citep{nhu2025tawm} demonstrates that $\dt$-conditioning can be highly effective within the TD-MPC2 framework \citep{hansen2024tdmpc2}.  By conditioning the world model on $\dt$, TAWM achieves variable-rate planning that adapts temporal resolution to task demands and delivers state-of-the-art performance without value overestimation.  This success might appear to contradict our finding that $\dt$-conditioning induces CIVO.  The discrepancy is fully explained by the architectural difference between MPC and imagination-based actor-critic methods.
15	
16	TD-MPC2 is an MPC architecture that optimizes action sequences directly on model rollouts via the cross-entropy method, without training a value function on imagined trajectories.  When $\dt > 1$, the world model inevitably loses some predictive fidelity, but this error remains bounded because the agent re-plans from real observed states at every decision point.  Model errors at larger temporal strides are corrected before they can compound, and no value function is trained on the imprecise predictions.  There is therefore no channel through which systematic bias can be internalized and amplified.
17	
18	In DreamerV3, the architecture creates a closed feedback cycle: the RSSM generates imagined trajectories, the critic estimates values along these trajectories, and the actor optimizes against the critic's estimates.  When $\dt > 1$, the RSSM develops a fidelity gap (evidenced by the $2.78\times$ reward prediction disparity in Table~\ref{tab:rssm_fidelity}), and the observation decoder gradient pathway encodes $\dt$-specific spatial predictions that sustain this gap.  The critic, trained on these systematically biased imagined returns, develops inflated value estimates for $\dt > 1$ states.  The actor then preferentially selects actions that reach these overvalued states, which reinforces the bias and closes the CIVO loop.  This positive feedback mechanism has no counterpart in MPC, where no critic is trained on model outputs.
19	
20	The vulnerability is therefore specific to the imagination-based actor-critic architecture, not to $\dt$-conditioning itself.  MPC avoids value amplification through open-loop optimization with re-planning, which prevents model error from entering a self-reinforcing cycle.  This architectural distinction also clarifies why multiple vulnerability pathways exist within the imagination-based framework: both CIVO (Pathway~A, value-driven, entropy decreasing) and non-CIVO instability (Pathway~B, eval-driven, entropy increasing, \S\ref{sec:f6}) originate from the same closed-loop structure that MPC lacks entirely.
21	
22	\paragraph{Practical monitoring.}
23	The online detector achieves perfect sensitivity (3/3 true positives) with a false positive rate of 2/8 (25\%).  A clear timing separation emerges: all true positives trigger before 65K steps (mean 52K), while both false positives trigger after 85K steps (mean 95K).  This separation yields a practical deployment guideline where alerts before 70K steps indicate high-confidence CIVO onset, and later alerts require human inspection to distinguish genuine pathology from transient fluctuations.  The two false positive cases illustrate qualitatively different failure modes: case 009c exhibits genuine value-performance dissociation (a non-CIVO pathology where the alert retains diagnostic value), whereas case 009a reflects a transient evaluation dip from which the agent recovers to near-optimal performance (eval 966).  This distinction suggests the detector functions as a general value-health monitor rather than a CIVO-specific classifier.  The underlying signal (accelerating divergence between predicted value and realized performance) captures any sustained value-performance dissociation regardless of mechanistic origin, and the 009c case demonstrates that such dissociation is a useful early-warning signal even when the root cause is not CIVO.  The current thresholds were calibrated on eleven runs across three environments; generalization to different reward scales and training regimes requires further validation.
24

1	\section{Conclusion}
2	\label{sec:conclusion}
3	
4	We have presented a systematic factorial diagnostic of temporal abstraction in DreamerV3 across two continuous-control environments, identifying the combination of trained $\dt$-embedding and multi-rate data exposure as the causal factor behind conditioning-induced value overestimation (CIVO). The key findings are:
5	
6	\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
7	\item Every variable-rate imagination configuration degrades relative to the $\dt{=}1$ baseline, with degradation scaling monotonically with $\dt$.
8	\item A normalized value-to-eval threshold of $\nve \geq 1.5\times$ (35K+ window) achieves 11/12 CIVO classification ($n{=}12$, 91.7\%), with the single false positive arising from a mechanistically distinct non-CIVO collapse. The combination of trained $\dt$-embedding and multi-rate data exposure is the causal factor; unexposed, frozen, or removed embeddings prevent overestimation.
9	\item The RSSM reward head develops a $2.78\times$ prediction gap between $\dt{=}1$ and $\dt{=}2$ under trained conditioning, providing the systematic bias that drives critic overestimation.
10	\item The same CIVO trigger produces stochastic downstream outcomes (full collapse and transient CIVO with self-correction) across seeds of identical configurations.
11	\item Restricting imagination to $\dt{=}1$ does not fully prevent collapse: one of two seeds fails via a qualitatively distinct non-CIVO pathway (eval-driven with increasing entropy), demonstrating that the trained $\dt$-embedding creates vulnerability through multiple mechanisms.
12	\item A lightweight online detector that monitors the dynamics of the value-to-evaluation ratio identifies CIVO onset with 100\% sensitivity across three positive cases, with predictive detection (alert before performance degradation) in two of three. A timing guideline ($<$70K steps = high confidence) separates genuine CIVO from late-stage false positives.
13	\end{enumerate}
14	
15	The contrast with TAWM's success in MPC identifies the feedback architecture as the critical factor: $\dt$-conditioning succeeds when errors are contained by re-planning from real states, but fails when errors compound through imagination-based actor-critic bootstrapping.
16	
17	\paragraph{Limitations.}
18	Our primary factorial analysis focuses on Walker Walk; cross-environment evidence (Cheetah Run) is limited to a single seed. Both use a single world-model architecture (DreamerV3/RSSM). Generalization to other environments and architectures, particularly transformer-based world models such as DreamerV4, remains an open question. The $\nve$ threshold ($1.5\times$, 35K+ window) is sensitive to value overestimation broadly but not perfectly specific to CIVO (11/12, one non-CIVO false positive); generalization to other tasks and architectures is pending validation. The detector's thresholds were calibrated on eleven runs across three environments; generalization to different reward scales and architectures requires further validation.
19	
20	\paragraph{Future directions.}
21	Our findings suggest three avenues. First, hierarchical temporal abstraction at the representation level (as in THICK and Hieros) may avoid the flat-conditioning failure mode by maintaining separate dynamics for each temporal scale. Second, gradient decomposition reveals that gradient importance is decoupled from magnitude: the reward head provides the largest share (38--49\%) but reward-only SGS fails, while the observation decoder channel (16--22\%) carries the critical $\dt$-specific information driving the fidelity gap. Full-pathway gradient stopping \sgsclaim{} (seed~1 eval \sgseval{}, seed~2 collapsed), indicating that cutting the observation decoder gradient pathway is necessary but not sufficient; the 50\% prevention rate points to redundant mechanisms in CIVO's feedback loop that future interventions must address jointly. Third, extending this diagnostic framework to transformer-based world models and continuous-control benchmarks would clarify whether CIVO is RSSM-specific or a broader vulnerability of temporal conditioning in imagination-based RL. Fourth, our findings suggest that freezing the temporal embedding while allowing the gate mechanism to learn (untrained embedding with adaptive horizon selection) may decouple the benefits of temporal abstraction from the CIVO vulnerability, a direction we are actively investigating.
22

1	Temporal abstraction via variable-rate imagination is a natural extension of world-model reinforcement learning, yet we find that every variable-rate configuration of DreamerV3 degrades performance, despite the success of identical $\Delta t$-conditioning in MPC-based methods. Through factorial diagnostics on two continuous-control tasks (Walker Walk, Cheetah Run), we identify the combination of trained temporal embedding and multi-rate data exposure as the causal factor and characterize the resulting failure mode: \emph{conditioning-induced value overestimation} (CIVO). The trained embedding enables the RSSM reward head to develop a $2.78\times$ prediction gap between $\Delta t{=}1$ and $\Delta t{=}2$, which the critic internalizes as optimistic values. This mechanism universally degrades performance to below 30\% of baseline across all three tested seeds ($n{=}3$), with two progressing toward full collapse and one self-correcting to a stable but degraded state. Gradient decomposition reveals that despite the reward head providing the largest gradient contribution (38--49\%), the observation decoder channel (16--22\%) carries the critical $\Delta t$-specific spatial information that drives the fidelity gap. Full-pathway gradient stopping partially prevents CIVO but succeeds in only 50\% of cases; this exposes additional mechanisms beyond gradient-mediated co-adaptation. A lightweight online detector that monitors value-to-evaluation ratio dynamics identifies CIVO onset with 100\% sensitivity (3/3 cases) and provides predictive warning before performance degradation in 2/3 cases, which supports early intervention without a reference baseline. The contrast with MPC-based methods identifies the feedback architecture (imagination-based bootstrapping versus re-planning) as the structural factor that transforms manageable model imprecision into pathological value dynamics.
2

1	\section{Introduction}
2	\label{sec:introduction}
3	
4	TAWM \citep{nhu2025tawm} shows that conditioning a world model on step size $\dt$ yields consistent gains within TD-MPC2's MPC framework \citep{hansen2024tdmpc2}. Can the same $\dt$-conditioning bring temporal abstraction to imagination-based actor-critic methods like DreamerV3 \citep{hafner2023dreamerv3}, where policies are trained entirely in imagined rollouts?
5	
6	We find that it cannot. Every variable-rate configuration we test degrades performance catastrophically: fixed $\dt{=}2$ collapses to $14\%$ of baseline, fixed $\dt{=}4$ never exceeds $19\%$ of baseline, and a learned Gumbel-Softmax gate collapses to $11\%$. Through a factorial analysis on Walker Walk \citep{tassa2018dmcontrol}, we isolate the combination of a \emph{trained} $\dt$-embedding and multi-rate data exposure as the causal factor within the factorial design tested. This trained-and-exposed embedding enables the RSSM reward head to develop a $2.78\times$ prediction gap between $\dt{=}1$ and $\dt{=}2$, which the critic internalizes as optimistic value estimates, a failure mode we term \emph{conditioning-induced value overestimation} (CIVO). A $\nve \geq 1.5\times$ threshold (35K+ window) achieves 11/12 CIVO classification ($n{=}12$, single environment), with one non-CIVO false positive, a failure mode analogous to delusional bias \citep{lu2018nondelusional} that arises from model imprecision amplified by learned temporal conditioning. Gradient decomposition reveals a non-obvious mechanism: the reward head contributes the largest gradient share (38--49\%) but does not encode $\dt$-specific structural information, while the observation decoder channel (16--22\%) carries the critical spatial predictions that drive the RSSM fidelity gap. Reward-only gradient stopping fails (NVE $10.42\times$) despite targeting the largest pathway; full-pathway SGS that removes observation decoder gradients from the temporal embedding \sgsclaim{} (eval \sgseval{} vs.\ collapse at 40.8), revealing that this intervention is necessary but not sufficient, as the 50\% prevention rate exposes additional mechanisms beyond gradient-mediated co-adaptation.
7	
8	Four further findings complicate the picture: (1)~expanded seed analysis ($n{=}3$) confirms that the same CIVO trigger universally degrades performance to below 30\% of baseline, with 2/3 of seeds progressing toward full collapse at variable onset timing and 1/3 self-correcting to a stable but degraded state; (2)~restricting imagination to $\dt{=}1$ while retaining the trained embedding does not prevent collapse, with one of two seeds failing via a qualitatively distinct non-CIVO pathway (evaluation-driven, increasing entropy); (3)~the contrast with TAWM identifies the feedback architecture (imagination-based bootstrapping versus MPC re-planning) as the structural factor that transforms manageable model imprecision into pathological value dynamics; and (4)~a lightweight four-condition rule-based monitor that tracks value-to-evaluation ratio dynamics achieves 100\% sensitivity for CIVO detection (3/3 cases) with predictive warning before performance degradation in 2/3 cases, which supports early intervention without a reference baseline run.
9
